sec: Medullary sponge kidney: features, pathogenesis & triad · p791

items.q: Medullary sponge kidney is a ciliopathy.
opts: False — it is not a ciliopathy but an acquired disease
True — it is one of the four ciliopathies
False — it is a hereditary autosomal dominant disease
items.exp: Medullary sponge kidney is explicitly stated to be not a ciliopathy and is an acquired disease. (Book p791)

items.q: Medullary sponge kidney is an acquired disease of middle age, usually seen at:
items.exp: Medullary sponge kidney: acquired disease usually seen at 30–50 years (middle age). (Book p791)

items.q: Which statement about the sex distribution of medullary sponge kidney is correct as printed?
opts: Female > male in India (m = f overall)
items.exp: Medullary sponge kidney: female > male in India (m = f overall). (Book p791)

items.q: Medullary sponge kidney carries no risk of CKD.
opts: False — it invariably progresses to ESRD
False — it causes CKD in 25% of patients
items.exp: Medullary sponge kidney: no risk for CKD. (Book p791)

items.q: Complete the sequence in medullary sponge kidney — 1) Primary event  2) Collecting-duct change  3) Cyst number … A) Dilated spongy medullary and papillary collecting ducts  B) Few cysts in the medulla  C) Malformation of the terminal collecting duct
items.exp: Pathogenesis of medullary sponge kidney: malformation of the terminal collecting duct leads to dilated spongy medullary and papillary collecting ducts with a few cysts in the medulla. (Book p791)

items.q: Fill up: In medullary sponge kidney, the malformation involves the ______ collecting duct.
items.exp: MSK pathogenesis: malformation of the terminal collecting duct → dilated spongy medullary and papillary collecting ducts with a few medullary cysts. (Book p791)

items.q: Match the medullary sponge kidney triad as shown in the triangle — 1) Stones  2) Infection  3) Bleeding … A) Recurrent stones due to distal RTA → hypercalciuria  B) Recurrent UTI  C) Recurrent haematuria
items.exp: The MSK triad: recurrent stones (due to distal renal tubular acidosis → hypercalciuria), recurrent UTI and recurrent haematuria. (Book p791)

items.q: A 42-year-old woman has repeated calcium stones and urinary infections. Work-up shows distal renal tubular acidosis with hypercalciuria. Which disease's classic triad is this?
items.exp: MSK triad: recurrent stones due to distal RTA → hypercalciuria, recurrent UTI and recurrent haematuria. (Book p791)

items.q: Fill up: In medullary sponge kidney, recurrent stones result from distal renal tubular ______ with hypercalciuria.
items.exp: MSK stone formation is due to distal RTA → hypercalciuria. (Book p791)

items.q: All but one of the following make up the classical triad of medullary sponge kidney. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: The MSK triad is recurrent stones (distal RTA → hypercalciuria), recurrent UTI and recurrent haematuria. (Book p791)
